title: A predictive decoder for the regulatory genome

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a reliable quantitative decoder that predicts how DNA sequence regulates molecular activity in a specified cellular context. Given a genome or a set of sequence changes, together with the cell type, state and conditions to be modeled, it would predict which genes change their expression, how RNA splicing changes and how associated chromatin measurements respond. AlphaGenome provides a substantial technical foundation for this goal, but the broad capability described here has not been demonstrated by the supplied evidence.

Proposed scope: The decoder would connect nearby and distant regulatory elements to their molecular consequences and predict effects in previously unseen individual genomes. It would also handle structural variants and combinations of variants, including cases where their joint effect differs from the sum of their separate effects. Those latter capabilities remain explicit targets of this concept; the supplied evidence does not establish their performance or demonstrate that no existing method can address them. Cellular context is part of the prediction specification, rather than an outcome assumed to be uniquely determined by sequence.

significance.text: If broadly reliable, this capability would make much of the noncoding genome functionally interpretable: researchers could predict which genes a regulatory change affects, in which contexts and by how much. Integrating expression, splicing and chromatin predictions could help distinguish different molecular routes from a sequence change to an observed effect. The supplied manuscript illustrates this value through its reported reconstruction of oncogenic TAL1 variant effects. Such examples establish a technical basis for the ambition, rather than demonstrating comprehensive regulatory decoding.

Conditional downstream possibilities include prioritizing regulatory variants for experiments, selecting informative perturbations and designing sequence changes with desired molecular effects. Reliable prediction of variant combinations would be especially valuable when an individual genome contains many changes whose effects cannot safely be inferred one at a time. These are projected uses of a decoder meeting the proposed scope, not achievements established by the supplied record.

The analogy to reading molecular instructions has limits. Predictive functional interpretation would not by itself supply a complete causal explanation of every regulatory process. Nor would accurate molecular predictions automatically establish disease risk or identify an effective treatment. The manuscript explicitly places broader phenotypes beyond its direct sequence-to-function scope because they involve gene function, development and environmental factors. Clinical prediction and treatment selection would require additional biological models, relevant patient information and separate validation.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unresolved capability is dependable quantitative prediction of regulatory consequences across genomes and specified cellular contexts. The AlphaGenome manuscript identifies particular difficulties with distal regulatory elements more than 100 kilobases away, tissue-specific patterns across contexts and condition-specific variant effects. It also reports that personal-genome prediction had not yet been benchmarked. These are documented limitations at the manuscript’s reporting time; they do not establish the absence of a solution throughout the field at a later date.

Engineering synthesis: A broadly useful decoder must connect distant regulatory signals to the correct target genes while preserving quantitative accuracy, and it must represent enough cellular context to distinguish responses to the same sequence in different states or conditions. It must also generalize from its training and benchmark settings to unseen genomes. A long input window alone does not demonstrate that all relevant distant influences have been captured or assigned correctly.

Proposed extensions introduce additional barriers. Structural variants can change the arrangement of regulatory elements and genes, while multiple variants may have interacting effects. A decoder claiming these capabilities would need to represent and evaluate those changes explicitly, rather than relying on performance for isolated variants. It would also need useful uncertainty estimates that identify where predictions are dependable and where a new genome, perturbation or cellular condition exceeds the demonstrated range. These requirements follow from the proposed scope; their field-wide state is not established by the supplied manuscript.

current_state.text: In the supplied AlphaGenome manuscript, the model predicts multiple regulatory measurements and variant effects from 1-megabase DNA segments. Its authors report matching or exceeding the strongest respective available external models on 24 of 26 variant-effect evaluations. This is substantial reported benchmark performance across the evaluated tasks, not evidence of reliable prediction for every regulatory mechanism, complete personal genome or combination of variants.

The manuscript’s Discussion describes remaining challenges in regulation by elements more than 100 kilobases away, tissue-specific patterns and condition-specific variant effects. It explicitly states that personal-genome prediction had not yet been benchmarked. Its reported TAL1 example supports integrated molecular interpretation in a particular setting, while the broader goal of predicting combined changes in real genomes across contexts remains unestablished by the supplied evidence. The review also does not establish performance for structural variants or interacting variants.

The supplied review verifies the manuscript’s identity from its content and directly supports the scientific statements above using saved extracted text. That extraction is partial: it contains 120,000 characters, truncates during page 31 and omits later material. The relevant abstract and Discussion passages were available to the reviewer, but the record does not support conclusions about omitted material. This account relies on that supplied review and does not imply a new inspection of the PDF.

The research associates the manuscript with January 28, 2026 and DOI 10.1038/s41586-025-10014-0, but the validated review did not verify that publication date or DOI association. The source index records retrieval on November 11, 2026; retrieval is not a publication date. Because the supplied freshness record is empty, the evidence does not establish field-wide status on November 1, 2026 or identify subsequent advances. These bibliographic and coverage limits leave the manuscript’s supported reported results intact.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: Before experimental results are available, predict expression, splicing and chromatin responses for diverse unseen human genomes and engineered variant combinations across several explicitly specified cell types, states and conditions. Include distant regulatory perturbations and structural variants because they remain within this concept’s scope. The evaluation should test both individual changes and combinations, allowing direct assessment of whether the model captures joint effects.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed evaluation requirements: Independent laboratories would measure molecular effect sizes and compare them with predictions, including predicted null effects. The protocol would prespecify accuracy, coverage and uncertainty-calibration thresholds, together with the measurements and comparisons used to assess them. No numerical thresholds are supplied here, and these requirements are proposed criteria rather than established community standards. Successful uncertainty estimates should reflect observed prediction errors across the evaluated contexts.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed evaluation requirements

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: Independent evaluations should reproduce performance on held-out genomes and perturbations, report failures as well as successes and state the cellular contexts and variant classes covered. A convincing result would establish demonstrated breadth within those boundaries; finite tests could not establish literal universality. Claims about disease prediction or treatment selection would require separate demonstrations connecting molecular predictions to biological and clinical outcomes.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: BIF-04, General reconstruction of causal cellular networks, has the closest explicit overlap. BIF-01 predicts molecular consequences of regulatory sequence in context, whereas BIF-04 seeks causal relationships among cellular components. A decoder could generate hypotheses or predicted perturbation responses for network reconstruction, but predictive accuracy alone would not establish a complete causal network. BIF-03, A transferable, predictive virtual cell, has broader scope: regulatory decoding could supply one component of a model that also represents other cellular processes.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-02, Predictive molecular dynamics from biological sequence, and BIF-09, Proteome-scale prediction of molecular interactions and affinities, concern molecular behavior that could help explain regulatory mechanisms. BIF-01 instead targets regulatory molecular outputs from genomic sequence and context. BIF-06, A general decoder for unknown gene and protein functions, addresses what gene products do; identifying the consequences of changing their regulation does not by itself determine all of those functions.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-05, Computer-aided design of functional whole genomes, and BIF-13, Predictive design of functional genetic circuits and pathways, could use a regulatory decoder to evaluate proposed designs. Their goals also require choosing and constructing functional systems. BIF-01 supplies a prediction capability, which would contribute to design without completing whole-genome, circuit or pathway engineering.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-07, Computational reconstruction of organism-scale molecular maps, concerns the organization of molecular information across an organism, while BIF-08, Reliable reconstruction and forecasting of single-cell fates, concerns cellular trajectories. Regulatory decoding could inform both, but predicting sequence-dependent molecular changes is narrower than reconstructing an organism-scale map or forecasting a cell’s eventual fate.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-11, Accessible, uncertainty-aware assembly of complex genomes, could provide sequence inputs for regulatory prediction, but reconstructing a genome and interpreting its regulatory consequences are distinct capabilities. BIF-12, Strain-resolved discovery and functional profiling of microbial communities, addresses community composition and function; the present concept’s proposed demonstrations focus on human genomes and specified cellular contexts. BIF-10, A broadly capable autonomous bioinformatics discovery system, could incorporate a regulatory decoder as a specialized tool, while adding broader capabilities for autonomous investigation.

unresolved_issues: The supplied evidence does not establish field-wide progress or whether the proposed gap remained open on November 1, 2026.
The manuscript’s claimed January 28, 2026 publication date and association with DOI 10.1038/s41586-025-10014-0 remain unverified.
The extraction truncates during page 31; later material was unavailable to the supplied review.
Performance for structural variants and interacting variants, and the field-wide limitations for those cases, remain unestablished by the supplied evidence.

The operational representation of cellular state and environmental conditions is unspecified; the supplied evidence supports context-specific challenges but does not establish a universal claim about sequence sufficiency.
Completion requires selecting numerical acceptance thresholds, genome and context coverage, measurement protocols and practical resource limits; none are resolved by the supplied record.
